land.text: the Kastamonu country held by the Chobanids

predecessors.note: The Anatolian beyliks table gives 'Chobanid Beylik, Founder: Husam al-Din Choban | Kastamonu (preceding the Candars) | 1211-1309'. No page opened says who held Kastamonu in 1211 or dates a handover: the Kastamonu Province page has the region 'under the hegemony of the Seljuq dynasty' (placed in the 11th century) and then 'Çobanoğlu and Jandarid beyliks', undated. sultanate-of-rum is the reading that the Seljuks of Rum were the overlords the Chobanids arose under (confidence 2).

land.text: the Kastamonu country conquered by Süleyman I Candar, who made it his seat

successors.note: Candar infobox: 'Eflani 1291-1309; Kastamonu 1309-1398'; text: 'Following the death of Şemseddin Yaman Candar, his son Süleyman I conquered the neighboring province of Kastamonu' (no year) and 'The province had previously been under the rule of the Çobanoğulları'. The Candar state at Eflani is Cliopatria's Beylik of Isfendiyar row (same Wikipedia article), so from 1309 the land is drawn in the beylik-of-isfendiyar dossier, which should list 'Kastamonu' in its cliopatria_names.

region.text: the Kastamonu country of the Chobanid beylik

ledger.note: 1211: Husam al-Din Choban founds the Chobanid beylik at Kastamonu. Beyliks table: 'Chobanid Beylik, Founder: Husam al-Din Choban | Kastamonu (preceding the Candars) | 1211-1309'. The year is the table's; the page has no prose on the Chobanids, and the extent is Cliopatria's 1305 shape projected back. The Candar page confirms 'The province had previously been under the rule of the Çobanoğulları'.

1309: the Candar state, until then at Eflani, takes Kastamonu from the Chobanids and makes it its seat. Candar page: 'Following the death of Şemseddin Yaman Candar, his son Süleyman I conquered the neighboring province of Kastamonu' (no year in the text); infobox 'Eflani 1291-1309; Kastamonu 1309-1398', reign table 'Suleiman I Pasha 1309-1339'. The year rests on the infobox and the beyliks table's end of the Chobanids; the Kastamonu Province page (tried for the date) gives no year and no conquest. Cliopatria's Beylik of Isfendiyar row is this Candar state.
1309: the Chobanid beylik at Kastamonu ends (beyliks table 1211-1309); its land passes to the Candars of Eflani.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary of the Chobanid beylik; the whole life is the Cliopatria 1305 shape, approximate, and its limits towards Sinop and the Candar core at Eflani are not sourced.

notes: Row identity: Cliopatria's 'Kastamonu' (Wikipedia title the city, Wikidata Q155915) is split at 1309. Until 1309 it is the Chobanid (Çobanoğulları) beylik at Kastamonu, 1211-1309 on one beyliks-table row; this dossier is that state only. From 1309 Kastamonu is the seat of the Candar state of Yaman Candar and Süleyman I (infobox 'Eflani 1291-1309; Kastamonu 1309-1398'), which is Cliopatria's Beylik of Isfendiyar row (same Wikipedia article, Eflani/Safranbolu); the Candar realm is therefore one state, drawn in the beylik-of-isfendiyar dossier, and this row's shapes kastamonu_1314, kastamonu_1323 and kastamonu_1333 are marked wrong here with the pointer 'Candar realm 1309-1343: reviewed in beylik-of-isfendiyar'. The beylik-of-isfendiyar author should list 'Kastamonu' in cliopatria_names, review the 1309-1313 years of kastamonu_1305 and the shapes 1314-1343, carry the Candar annexation of Sinop (1322 on the beyliks table; see beylik-of-sinop) and the 1343 'bookkeeping' end of Cliopatria's Kastamonu row (no event on the Candar page; Kastamonu stays the seat to 1398). Thin: the date and manner of the Candar conquest of Kastamonu. The Candar text gives no year ('his son Süleyman I conquered the neighboring province of Kastamonu'); 1309 is the infobox's capital change plus the beyliks table's end of the Chobanids. The Kastamonu Province page was opened to find it and has only undated 'Çobanoğlu and Jandarid beyliks' and the Ottoman conquest of 1392. The Chobanid rulers, the founder's dates and the beylik's relation to Rum (and, after 1243, to the Ilkhanate) are on no page opened; the Persian Chobanids article is unrelated. The 1211 start is the one table row. The Ilkhanate dossier (ia-02) carries vassal events with counterpart kastamonu for 1305-1335; for 1309-1335 they should name beylik-of-isfendiyar (the Candar page: Süleyman 'reigned under the authority of the Ilkhanate ... until the death of their ruler Abu Sa'id'). The Chobanids here are the beylik of Kastamonu, not Cliopatria's Chobanids (Tabriz, 1344-1362).
